source.title: Three Factors Influencing Minima in SGD
source.authors: Stanislaw Jastrzebski; Zachary Kenton; Devansh Arpit; Nicolas Ballas; Asja Fischer; Yoshua Bengio; A. Storkey

record.tranche_reason: Tests memorization with partially corrupted labels while varying SGD noise; it does not test fitting a completely random labeling or the other listed interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that its MLPs reached the stated memorization threshold, and describes validation performance after memorization. Figure 6 is the only source for the separate performance values; no precise values are reconstructed. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: Section 3.4 bears on V4: MNIST MLPs memorize randomly corrupted labels at 25% and 50% corruption, while held-out accuracy is lower at 50%. It does not test V1's completely random labeling.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes Section 3.4: higher SGD noise improves generalization after memorization, and Hessian norm correlates negatively with η/S (r = −0.58, p ≤ 0.001). The broader conclusion is that learning rate, batch size, and gradient covariance influence SGD's final minima; higher η/S tends to yield wider minima and better generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Varies the learning-rate-to-batch-size ratio and momentum while fitting MNIST with 25% or 50% randomly replaced labels; it does not reproduce the original fully random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization after memorization varies with η/S; the experiments include momentum 0.0 and 0.9 and label-corruption fractions of 25% and 50%.

fits_no_version.finding: Higher learning-rate-to-batch-size ratios improve held-out accuracy after memorization at fixed label-corruption fractions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD noise influences generalization even among networks that memorize corrupted training labels.

record.problems: The memorization result is presented in a figure without tabulated performance values. The paper tests only 25% and 50% random-label fractions, not complete random labeling; no uncertainty is stated for these Figure 6 results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results on the listed claim versions were reported. The broader SGD dynamics, curvature, generalization and cyclic-schedule experiments concern other behaviors and were left out.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, chance test performance, and fitting without changes to architecture or training hyperparameters.
Training-time comparison with true labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
A continuous or sufficiently dense corruption sweep, the uncorrupted and fully random endpoints, and steady degradation toward chance across that sweep.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and augmentation on memorization and true-label generalization.
Learning real patterns before noisy labels; no separate learning trajectories are reported.

record.verdict_notes: The original V1 limits_scope verdict mistakes an untested condition for a demonstrated limitation. No failure to memorize is reported. Figure 6's extracted layout is ambiguous, so its panel positions should not override the explicit corruption and momentum conditions.

versions.untested_parts: Tests memorization of randomly relabeled examples at 25% and 50% label corruption, not a fully random labeling of the entire training set; test error at chance is not reported.
Training time or convergence speed relative to true labels is not reported.
Shuffled pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
The fraction of corrupted labels is not swept from none to all, and a steady rise in test error with that fraction is not reported.
Weight decay, dropout and data augmentation are not tested for their effects on fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
The order in which real patterns and noisy labels are learned is not measured.

rows.subject: MLP (256 hidden units; similar to the one used by Arpit & et al. (2017))
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with 25% of training labels replaced with random labels; evaluated after memorization, defined as at least 99.9% accuracy on random labels.

conditions.value: varied over a grid of η/S

rows.measure: Test accuracy after memorizing the training set
rows.note: The text says larger SGD noise leads to better generalization after memorization; the figure gives no tabulated values. The reported corruption is partial, not a fully random labeling of the entire set.
rows.check: Replace V1 with V4. Record the reported ≥99.9% accuracy on random training labels alongside held-out accuracy. Partial coverage of corruption fractions is not a partial effect. Figure 6 labels the held-out measure test accuracy, although the prose calls it validation performance.

relationships.condition: MNIST MLP, 25% versus 50% label corruption, momentum 0 or 0.9, across the reported learning-rate/batch-size grid
relationships.reason: R1–R4 report memorization at ≥99.9% accuracy on random training labels; Figure 6 shows lower held-out accuracy at 50% than at 25% corruption. This supports the measured portion of V4, without establishing the full degradation curve.
relationships.display_finding: Random training labels were memorized with at least 99.9% accuracy, while held-out accuracy was lower at 50% corruption than at 25%.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
